newsitem.title: ESTONIA: SOCCER-SCOTLAND'S PLEA FOR EARLY KICK-OFF VETOED BY FIFA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SCOTLAND'S PLEA FOR EARLY KICK-OFF VETOED BY FIFA.

text.p: Scotland have lost their fight to have Wednesday's World Cup qualifier against Estonia brought forward because of worries that the floodlighting at the Kadriorg Stadium is inadequate.
After inspecting the lighting with Scottish officials on Tuesday, FIFA delegate Jean-Marie Gantenbein ruled the match would go ahead at 1845 local time.
The Scots had wanted to play in the afternoon.

"I am not happy with the lighting and do not feel it is sufficient," said Scotland coach Craig Brown after inspecting two temporary floodlight stanchions which were at a different height from two permanent stanchions.
"It is a gloomy, eerie atmosphere and there is clearly a problem. It is the worst lighting I can recall for an international match."
After losing his first appeal, Brown said he would "register the strongest possible complaint" to FIFA as quickly as he could.
"If there is no change then we will have to try and prepare accordingly."
Estonian soccer authorities were reluctant to have the match played earlier because of contractual obligations over live television coverage.
Estonian F.A. secretary Hiner Leppainen said: "The TV coverage is worth a lot of money to us but we have paid a lot of money, too, for the lights. We need cash to develop our game and stadium here."
